name: Topolograph Docker
what_it_is: A containerized network topology visualization and what-if analysis platform that collects Link State Database (LSDB) information from routers running OSPF or IS-IS and renders an interactive graph. It also ships an MCP server so LLM agents can query topology, calculate paths, and monitor routing events via API.
components: flask — Python/Flask web application and REST API backend (vadims06/topolograph:latest)
mongodb — Persistent store for topology data (mongo:4.2)
mcp-server — Model Context Protocol server exposing Topolograph API to AI agents (vadims06/topolograph-mcp-server:v1.0.0)
webserver — Nginx reverse proxy serving the UI on configurable port
flask-create-creds-from-env — One-shot init container that seeds API credentials from environment variables
protocols: OSPF (OSPFv2) — topology collection via NAPALM device login and LSDB retrieval
OSPFv3 — mentioned in description as supported
IS-IS — topology collection and event monitoring
BGP-LS — listed in project description; not explicitly documented in README
measurement: Path calculation between any two nodes in the topology graph
Backup path analysis (loop-free alternates / failover paths)
Graph connectivity and node/edge status queries
Hostname resolution of OSPF Router IDs via configurable DNS server
configuration: TOPOLOGRAPH_PORT — HTTP port for the web UI (default 8080)
MCP_PORT — HTTP port for the MCP server (default 8000)
NAPALM_USERNAME / NAPALM_PASSWORD / NAPALM_PORT — credentials for device login to pull LSDB
DNS — IP address of DNS server used to resolve router IDs to hostnames
TOPOLOGRAPH_WEB_API_USERNAME_EMAIL / TOPOLOGRAPH_WEB_API_PASSWORD — API and web login credentials
TOPOLOGRAPH_WEB_API_AUTHORISED_NETWORKS — IP whitelist for API request sources
MONGODB_DATABASE / MONGODB_USERNAME / MONGODB_PASSWORD / MONGODB_HOSTNAME — MongoDB connection settings
NETBOX_URL / NETBOX_RO_TOKEN — optional NetBox integration for hostname enrichment (marked deprecated in README)
fault_injection: What-if analysis: the project description explicitly names 'what-if analysis' as a core feature, implying the ability to simulate link or node failures against the stored topology graph
No programmatic fault injection API is documented in the README or docker-compose; fault scenarios appear to be exploratory via the web UI or MCP path-calculation tools
modes: Interactive web UI mode — browser-based topology visualization at http://localhost:8080/
REST API mode — authenticated JSON API consumed by scripts or external tools (Swagger host configurable)
MCP agent mode — AI/LLM agents connect to http://localhost:8000/mcp for structured network queries
Automated install mode — install.sh script pulls images, configures .env, and starts all services
constraints: MongoDB is pinned to version 4.2; README notes a required upgrade path to 4.4.29 before moving further, indicating version lock risk
NAPALM-based LSDB collection requires SSH/API access to each monitored router with valid credentials — no passive-only or SNMP collection path documented
API source IP whitelisting (TOPOLOGRAPH_WEB_API_AUTHORISED_NETWORKS) must be configured before API calls succeed; misconfiguration silently blocks access
MCP server authenticates via API token passed by the agent; token provisioning is manual and not automated in the default setup
NetBox integration is deprecated (struck through in README); hostname enrichment depends solely on DNS resolution
BGP-LS support is claimed in the project description but absent from the README and docker-compose environment variables
docker_services: flask — port 5000 (internal only), image vadims06/topolograph:latest, networks: frontend + backend
mongodb — port 27017:27017, image mongo:4.2, volume mongodbdata:/data/db, network: backend
mcp-server — port ${MCP_PORT:-8000}:8000, image vadims06/topolograph-mcp-server:v1.0.0, network: frontend
webserver — port ${TOPOLOGRAPH_PORT:-8080}:${TOPOLOGRAPH_PORT:-8080}, built from ./webserver/Dockerfile, volume nginxdata, depends on flask + mcp-server, network: frontend
flask-create-creds-from-env — ephemeral init container, same image as flask, bind-mounts ./init/create_credentials_from_env.py
notable_absences: No BGP-LS collector or configuration documented despite being listed as a supported protocol
No built-in watcher/collector service in docker-compose — external OSPF/IS-IS watcher agents (referenced by install.sh) are a separate component not included in this repo
No TLS/HTTPS configuration for the web UI or MCP server in the provided compose file
No health checks defined for any service in docker-compose.yml
No rate limiting or request throttling documented for the MCP or REST API
No backup or restore procedure for the MongoDB volume documented
